questions.stem: What is excretion in living organisms?

options.text: Excretion is the process of digesting food in the body.
Excretion only refers to passing urine from the body.
The biological process involved in the removal of these harmful metabolic wastes from the body is called excretion.
Excretion is only the removal of gaseous wastes like CO2.

questions.source_quote: The biological process involved in the removal of these harmful metabolic wastes from the body is called excretion.
questions.explanation: The quoted sentence defines excretion as the removal of harmful metabolic wastes, not just urine or gases.

questions.stem: Which organs make up the human excretory system?

options.text: Only the kidneys and bladder.
Lungs and heart only.
A pair of kidneys, a pair of ureters, a urinary bladder and a urethra.
The stomach, intestines, and pancreas.

questions.source_quote: The excretory system of human beings (Fig. 5.13) includes a pair of kidneys, a pair of ureters, a urinary bladder and a urethra.
questions.explanation: The quote lists all the organs that form the human excretory system.

questions.stem: What happens to most of the filtrate produced in the kidneys each day?

options.text: None of the filtrate is re-absorbed.
All the filtrate leaves the body as urine.
The filtrate is converted into blood cells.
Most of the filtrate is re-absorbed in the kidney tubules.

questions.source_quote: However, the volume actually excreted is only a litre or two a day, because the remaining filtrate is re- absorbed in the kidney tubules.
questions.explanation: The quote explains that most filtrate is re-absorbed, not excreted as urine.

questions.stem: Where is urine stored before it is passed out of the body?

options.text: In the urinary bladder.
In the lungs.
In the urethra.
In the kidneys.

questions.source_quote: Urine is stored in the urinary bladder until the pressure of the expanded bladder leads to the urge to pass it out through the urethra.
questions.explanation: The quote clearly states that urine is stored in the urinary bladder before being passed out.

questions.stem: How do plants get rid of some of their waste products?

options.text: By converting waste into food.
By excreting all waste through roots only.
By storing waste in leaves that fall off or in vacuoles.
By not producing any waste at all.

questions.source_quote: Many plant waste products are stored in cellular vacuoles. Waste products may be stored in leaves that fall off.
questions.explanation: The quote shows that plants store waste in vacuoles and leaves that fall off as a way to remove waste.
